transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Ryland Barton.
Authorities say at least two people were hospitalized today after a shooting at an elementary school
in Bend, Oregon, and the shooter was shot and killed.
Bend police spokesperson Sheila Miller says children were among the victims.
Authorities received a call about a shot fired into a car outside Silver Rail Elementary
and arrived on scene within minutes.
Miller says the shooter was taken down inside the school soon after police arrived.
The conditions of those injured were not immediately known.
The Justice Department is suing California to block state election officials from counting
mail-in ballots from suspected non-citizens, NPR's Ryan Lucas reports.
>> The Justice Department says it filed its lawsuit after election officials in California
failed to cross-check the state's voter rolls against a list of some 20,000 names of quote-unquote
likely non-citizens believed to have been sent vote-by-mail ballots.
The DOJ provided that list of names to state election officials earlier this week on an
encrypted thumb drive and gave them a 48-hour deadline to conduct a review.
In its lawsuit, the department is asking the court to block California from counting mail-in
ballots from what it calls likely non-citizens until voter citizenship can be determined.
Secretary of State rejected the DOJ's efforts, saying this week the department is trying
to unlawfully access protected voter data.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
>> Some Georgians say they plan to vote to check President Trump's power.
NPR's Mara Leison has more on a focus group of voters who backed Joe Biden in 2020 before
swinging to President Trump two years ago.
>> These voters feel betrayed.
They believed him when he said he would bring prices down and wouldn't get into any more
wars.
Now they say they're more economically anxious than they were before Trump took office.
Specifically, each one of them said they're things that they've cut back on, like eating
out or going on vacation.
And more importantly, they're drawing a direct line from the decisions that Trump has made
to raise tariffs or go to war and the struggles they're having to make ends meet.
>> NPR's Mara Leison reporting.
Officials in Southern California are preparing for wildfires with much of the region under
a red flag warning from member station LAist Lucas Brady Woods reports.
>> The risk is so high right now because of a mix of strong winds, dry vegetation and
low humidity.
If a fire breaks out under these conditions, it can easily spread out of control.
Similar factors drove the deadly Los Angeles wildfires in 2025.
Los Angeles Fire Department Captain Milo Cope says wind can spread embers over long distances.
>> They can fly up to a mile out and then drop down and because the weather is dry,
they drop down and they catch and they'll light that brush on fire ahead of us.
>> California Governor Gavin Newsom and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass have ordered extra
firefighting resources to high risk areas across the region.
For NPR News, I'm Lucas Brady Woods in Los Angeles.
>> US Stock Index is closed up today.
The Dow rose more than 1%.
This is NPR.
Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Celia Flores say torture allegations
against them are false.
They both pleaded not guilty after they were accused last week of leading a state-sponsored
repression effort to torture opponents and others, including three Americans.
A rewritten indictment says Maduro and Flores approved of torture techniques that included
beatings and electric shocks.
The world's leading manufacturers of cutting-edge microchips and the machines that make them
say business is good.
NPR's John Ruich reports quarterly results from Taiwan's TSMC and the Dutch company ASML
show no signs of the AI boom ending anytime soon.
>> Taiwan's TSMC says its profit surged 69% in the latest quarter, the sixth quarter in
a row of record earnings.
The company is the world's biggest contract chip maker and its fate hinges increasingly
on demand from companies buying chips for AI data centers.
It says that demand is very strong and increasing.
Meanwhile, the Dutch company ASML, which makes the complex printing tools that fabricate
cutting-edge chips, also reported strong earnings this week.
It says demand for its chip making machines is increasing, and it's trying to boost capacity
to meet it.
Despite all that, investors remain on edge about the flood of money going into AI, and
chip stocks have dipped in recent days.
John Ruich, NPR News.
>> The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration says the U.S. winter will likely be wetter
and warmer, but not necessarily snowier due to El Niño.
Scientists predict below normal snow in the Northeast, Great Lakes, Upper Midwest, and
Northern Rockies, but more in the Southeast, Southern Rockies, and Southwest.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon leaves two hospitalized; shooter killed
Justice Department sues California to block counting mail-in ballots from suspected non-citizens
Georgia focus group of 2020 Biden voters who switched to Trump expresses economic betrayal
Southern California under red flag warning; officials prepare for possible wildfires
Dow rises more than 1% as US stock indexes close higher
Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and wife Celia Flores plead not guilty to torture charges
TSMC and ASML report strong quarterly earnings, showing AI chip demand still rising
NOAA forecasts wetter, warmer US winter with El Niño, but not necessarily snowier
